description: The image displays three pie charts, each representing the distribution of different categories across three difficulty levels—easy, medium, and hard—associated with the performance of large language models on a geometric knowledge reasoning task. The first chart, labeled "easy," shows four segments: a teal section labeled "N" at 40.6%, a yellow section labeled "N–K+" at 45.9%, an orange section labeled "N–K−" at 10.1%, and a small red section labeled "N+K−" at 3.3%. The second chart, labeled "medium," features a teal "N" segment at 44.6%, a yellow "N–K+" segment at 44.3%, an orange "N–K−" segment at 7.2%, and a red "N+K−" segment at 3.9%. The third chart, labeled "hard," presents a teal "N" segment at 20.1%, a yellow "N–K+" segment at 36.2%, an orange "N–K−" segment at 36.8%, and a red "N+K−" segment at 7.0%. A legend on the right side of the image correlates the colors to the categories: teal for "N", yellow for "N–K+", orange for "N–K−", and red for "N+K−". Each pie chart has its respective label ("easy", "medium", "hard") positioned above it, and the percentage values are clearly labeled within each slice. The visual arrangement suggests a progression in difficulty, with the proportions of the different categories shifting across the three levels.
